stages.title: CITIZENSHIP AS LEGAL MEMBERSHIP: CITIZEN, ALIEN AND THE CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS MAP
stages.terms: Citizenship is the legally recognised membership of the Indian political community: it links allegiance and protection, allocates political voice and selected public offices, and remains principally statutory after the Constitution's commencement settlement.
stages.mechanism: It creates a reciprocal relation: the citizen owes allegiance to India, while the constitutional and statutory order recognises a bundle of civil and political entitlements.
stages.consequence: CONTENT CLASSIFICATION: CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS
stages.trap: India's rights map follows constitutional text, not a citizen-versus-alien slogan: Articles 14, 20, 21 and 25 protect persons; Articles 15, 16, 19 and 29 are citizen-specific; Article 30 speaks of minorities; and voting is statutory, not a Fundamental Right.
stages.answer: Citizenship is the legally recognised membership of the Indian political community: it links allegiance and protection, allocates political voice and selected public offices, and remains principally statutory after the Constitution's commencement settlement.
